minutes.headline: Screening committee met consultant Community Paradigm, set Oct 7 to approve the job profile, and debated the manager salary range.
minutes.summary: The Town Manager Screening Committee held its first working meeting with the search consultant, who laid out the process: interviews with the select board and department heads, a position statement, advertising, tiered candidate review, executive-session interviews and background checks. The committee set a meeting for October 7 at 6:30 to approve the position statement and discussed the advertised salary range, with the consultant to research and recommend a figure to the select board. Minutes of the August 19 meeting were moved and seconded, but the outcome of the vote is not clearly captured.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the August 19th, 2024 meeting
Adjourn the meeting (roll call taken: Chris, Tom and others said aye)

budget_items.topic: Town manager salary range for the ad
budget_items.what_was_said: Members and the consultant discussed where to set the advertised pay; the consultant suggested a figure with plus or minus, while a member said the select board mentioned a higher range. No official vote had been taken.
A member said this is not the place to save money on the search.
A member noted accountability to voters who just passed an override and questioned higher figures; another called the lower figure astronomically low for a top candidate.
The consultant cited nearby towns paying lower amounts and said the 495 belt pays more.
Members tried to recall the superintendent salary and the previous manager's total pay under a five-year contract; figures were unsure.

The consultant will research salary and bring a formal recommendation to the select board, targeting its October 1 meeting (possibly the 17th by Zoom).
Consultant to get department head contacts and have an email sent so staff can meet him; interviews with the five select board members to be scheduled.

List of people to be consulted agreed: police chief, fire chief, DPW, facilities, HR, superintendent, acting land use manager, building commissioner, Council on Aging, Parks, Finance Committee chair, library.
Executive-session minutes will refer to candidates by letter or number; at least two names, preferably three or more, go to the select board.

what_happened.line: The Town Manager Screening Committee set Monday, October 7 at 6:30 to review and approve the position statement for the search.
The search consultant will research the advertised salary range and bring a formal recommendation to the select board, targeting its October 1 meeting.
Members discussed where to set the advertised pay; no vote was taken, and views ranged from caution about voters to concern a low range would deter top candidates.
The committee agreed who the consultant will interview, from department heads and the superintendent to the Finance Committee chair, plus the five select board members.
Executive-session interviews will refer to candidates by letter or number, and at least two names, preferably three or more, go to the select board.

why_it_matters: The advertised pay range for town manager shapes who applies and what the position costs the town, and the committee had not settled it at this meeting.
The committee's process decides how many candidates reach the select board, which makes the final hiring choice for the town's top administrative post.
